paras: The killing of Bryson near Dardanelle, Arkansas, was the shooting of a man pursued by a posse in June 1888, whose body was found in the Arkansas River a few miles below Dardanelle on Sunday, June 10. He had been accused of attempting to assault the wife of a man named Shinn, and a dispatch from Little Rock said Shinn had raised the posse that caught him. The story ran as a brief wire item in papers from Indiana to Nebraska.

According to the reports, Bryson, whose first name and race were not given, attempted "a few days" before the discovery to "criminally assault" the wife of Dock Shinn. The Little Rock dispatch placed Shinn's home on the Arkansas River in Yell County and said the assault happened "one day last week."

After the alleged assault, Bryson was pursued by a posse. In the Little Rock account, Shinn himself organized the posse, which caught Bryson and then came back without him, giving "no explanation of his whereabouts." On Sunday, June 10, his body, "riddled with bullets," was found in the river a few miles below Dardanelle. The Little Rock dispatch added that weights had been attached to the feet.
No report of an inquest, arrest or prosecution appears in the coverage, and no follow-up story was found.

The first version came from Dardanelle as a special to the St. Louis Post-Dispatch, which a St. Louis wire relayed on June 11. On June 12 the Indianapolis Journal carried it among its "Telegraphic Brevities," the Telegram-Herald in Michigan under "Crime in Arkansas," the Wichita Eagle as "Found in the River," and the Wilmington Daily Republican in its news summary. These items stated the assault charge as fact but called the posse's role a supposition: "It is supposed he was overtaken, shot, and his body flung in the river."

A separate Little Rock dispatch, printed by the Beatrice Daily Express in Nebraska on June 13 as "A Husband's Terrible Revenge," was more direct, presenting the killing as the husband's retaliation. None of the reports mentioned race, and none commented on the killing beyond their headlines. The name appeared variously as Brysson, Bryson and Brison, and the husband as Dock, Dick or D. Shinn.

reader.title: Killing of Bryson near Dardanelle, Arkansas
bases: Every report says Bryson was pursued by a posse after an alleged assault and later found shot in the river; the Little Rock dispatch says the posse, organized by the woman's husband, caught him (A1, A2, A5).

Bryson was found shot to death after a privately organized posse pursued him over an alleged attempted assault, and the Little Rock dispatch says the posse caught him and returned without him (A1, A5); no article states the posse's size or says directly who fired, and the Dardanelle story only 'supposed' the posse killed him (A2).

Two apparently independent dispatches, one from Dardanelle via the St. Louis Post-Dispatch and one from Little Rock, agree on the alleged assault, the posse pursuit and the bullet-riddled body in the Arkansas River (A3, A5).

accounts.gist: The body was found riddled with bullets below Dardanelle after Bryson had been pursued by a posse; it was 'supposed' he was overtaken, shot and thrown in the river.

accounts.label: Little Rock dispatch
accounts.gist: Shinn organized a posse that caught Bryson; the posse came back without him and would not say where he was, and his body was later found in the river, shot and weighted at the feet.

framing.detail: Northern and western papers ran the Dardanelle story as a one-paragraph item in telegraphic or news-summary columns ('Crime in Arkansas', 'Found in the River'), stating the assault charge as fact and the killing as supposition.
The Little Rock version, headed 'A Husband's Terrible Revenge', framed the killing as the husband's retaliation without comment.
